skill.name: commit-message
skill.description: Format git commit messages combining Conventional Commits summary lines with Linux kernel-style bodies. Use when writing, reviewing, or formatting commit messages.
skill.summary: Format Git commit messages with Conventional Commit headers and clear, kernel-style bodies.
skill.author: Chemiseblanc

content.value_statement: Inconsistent commit messages make reviews and release notes harder to scan. This skill formats concise Conventional Commit summaries with clear 72-column bodies.
actual_capabilities: Creates summary lines using allowed Conventional Commit types.
Adds optional scopes and breaking change markers.
Writes body text focused on motivation and user impact.
Keeps summary and body line lengths within stated limits.
Removes trailers such as Signed-off-by, Reviewed-by, and Fixes.
limitations: Does not inspect Git history or diffs unless the host agent provides them.
Does not create commits or run Git commands by itself.
Does not validate project-specific commit policies beyond listed rules.
Does not preserve trailers because the skill explicitly omits them.

use_cases.title: Draft a Commit Message
use_cases.description: Turn a change summary into a concise Conventional Commit message with a useful body.

use_cases.title: Normalize Patch Submissions
use_cases.description: Rewrite long or inconsistent commit text before review while keeping the technical intent clear.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release History
use_cases.description: Create consistent commit text that is easier to read when building changelogs.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a commit message for these changes: [describe changes]. Use the commit-message skill.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a short change summary

prompt_templates.title: Commit With Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Format this as a Conventional Commit with scope [component]: [describe the change and motivation].
prompt_templates.scenario: A change affects one clear component

prompt_templates.title: Commit Body From Diff Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a commit message from these diff notes. Explain the reason, user impact, and any measurable improvement.
prompt_templates.scenario: A larger change needs a useful body

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this commit message against the skill rules, then rewrite it if needed: [paste message].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup before submitting a patch

output_examples.input: The parser now returns an empty result for blank input instead of failing.
output_examples.output:
fix(parser): handle empty input without panic

Blank input can appear when users submit optional fields. Returning an empty result keeps validation predictable and prevents avoidable request failures.

output_examples.input: OAuth2 PKCE support was added for mobile and browser clients.
output_examples.output:
feat(auth): add OAuth2 PKCE flow support

Mobile and browser clients cannot safely store client secrets. PKCE lets these clients authenticate without relying on the insecure implicit flow.

best_practices: Provide the diff summary and motivation before asking for a message.
Name the affected component so the scope can be accurate.
Mention user impact and measurable results for the body.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for trailers if the project requires this skill's no-trailer style.
Do not provide only file names without explaining behavior changes.
Do not use vague summaries such as update code or fix issue.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands?
faq.answer: No. It only gives formatting guidance for commit messages.

faq.question: Which commit style does it use?
faq.answer: It combines Conventional Commit summaries with clear, kernel-style body text.

faq.question: Can it write breaking-change messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the exclamation marker before the colon when a change is breaking.

faq.question: Does it include Signed-off-by trailers?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly tells users to omit commit trailers.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: A short change summary, affected component, reason for the change, and user impact work best.

faq.question: Can it review an existing message?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask it to check the message against the rules and rewrite it if needed.
